{{short description|Triangle center}}

In [[geometry]], the '''Exeter point''' is a special point associated with a plane [[triangle]]. It is a [[triangle center]]  and is designated as ''X''(22)<ref>{{cite web|last=Kimberling|first=Clark|title=Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers: X(22)|url=https://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/encyclopedia/ETC.html#X22|accessdate=24 May 2012}}</ref> in [[Clark Kimberling]]'s [[Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers]]. This was discovered in a computers-in-mathematics workshop at [[Phillips Exeter Academy]] in 1986.<ref name=Exeter>{{cite web|last=Kimberling|first=Clark|title=Exeter Point|url=https://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/tcenters/recent/exeter.html|accessdate=24 May 2012}}</ref> This is one of the recent triangle centers, unlike the classical triangle centers like [[centroid]], [[incenter]], and [[Steiner point (triangle)|Steiner point]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Kimberling|first=Clark|title=Triangle centers|url=http://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/tcenters/|accessdate=24 May 2012}}</ref>

==Definition==
[[File:Exeter point.svg|thumb|300px|
{{legend-line|solid black|Reference triangle {{math|△''ABC''}}}}
{{legend-line|dashed black 2px|[[Median (geometry)|Medians]] (concur at [[centroid]])}}
{{legend-line|solid cyan|[[Circumcircle]]}}
{{legend-line|solid #2fc437|Triangle {{math|△''A'B'C' ''}} formed by intersection of medians with circumcircle}}
{{legend-line|solid magenta|[[Tangential triangle]] {{math|△''DEF''}}}}
{{legend-line|solid red|Lines joining vertices of {{math|△''DEF''}} and {{math|△''A'B'C' ''}} (concur at '''Exeter point''')}}
]]

The Exeter point is defined as follows.<ref name=Exeter/><ref>{{cite web|last=Weisstein|first=Eric W.|title=Exeter Point|url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/ExeterPoint.html|publisher=From MathWorld--A Wolfram Web Resource|accessdate=24 May 2012}}</ref> 
*Let {{math|△''ABC''}} be any given triangle. 
*Let the [[Median (geometry)|medians]] through the vertices {{mvar|A}}, {{mvar|B}}, {{mvar|C}} meet the [[circumcircle]] of {{math|△''ABC''}} at {{mvar|A'}}, {{mvar|B'}}, {{mvar|C'}} respectively. 
*Let {{math|△''DEF''}} be [[tangential triangle|the triangle]] formed by the [[tangent]]s at {{mvar|A}}, {{mvar|B}}, {{mvar|C}} to the circumcircle of {{math|△''ABC''}}. (Let {{mvar|D}} be the vertex opposite to the side formed by the tangent at the vertex {{mvar|A}}, {{mvar|E}} be the vertex opposite to the side formed by the tangent at the vertex {{mvar|B}}, and {{mvar|F}} be the vertex opposite to the side formed by the tangent at the vertex {{mvar|C}}.) 
*The lines through {{mvar|DA'}}, {{mvar|EB'}}, {{mvar|FC'}} are [[concurrent lines|concurrent]]. The point of concurrence is the ''Exeter point'' of {{math|△''ABC''}}.

Put succinctly, the Exeter point is the [[perspector]] of the '''circummedial triangle''' and the [[tangential triangle]].

==Trilinear coordinates==
The [[trilinear coordinates]] of the Exeter point are

<math display=block>a(b^4 + c^4 - a^4) : b(c^4 + a^4 - b^4) : c(a^4 + b^4 - c^4)</math>

==Properties==
*The Exeter point of triangle ''ABC'' lies on the [[Euler line]] (the line passing through the [[centroid]], the [[orthocenter]], the [[de Longchamps point]], the [[Euler centre]]  and the [[circumcenter]]) of triangle ''ABC''. So there are 6 points collinear on a single line.
